name: Editorial Gallery
tagline: A printed cookbook opening spread translated into a calm, photo-led interface.
thesis: Paul's Cookbook should feel like a carefully art-directed personal volume before it feels like software: the masthead carries the identity, chapter dividers pace the collection, and every recipe reads as a plated photograph with quiet typographic facts underneath.

typography.display: Fraunces with Georgia fallback for the oversized masthead and chapter openers
typography.ui: Inter/system-ui for controls and readable bilingual body copy
typography.data: JetBrains Mono/ui-monospace for numerals, counts, prices, and index labels

moves: Treat the first viewport as a masthead spread: huge serif wordmark, quiet caption, and a single underlined search line.
Render category sections as cookbook chapters with oversized numerals, hairline rules, large names, and tracked recipe counts.
Make each card a plate: framed photo first, then full untruncated title and hairline-separated prep/price data below the image.
Move filters, category navigation, more links, and preferences into a right-side Contents / Index drawer with printed-book rules.
Use one restrained ink-blue accent against paper and ink, with a black-stock dark theme rather than a simple inversion.
Keep motion minimal: slow ink fades and a measured drawer slide, disabled for reduced-motion users.
tradeoffs: The two-column grid is intentionally preserved on desktop, which shows fewer recipes per row but keeps the signature gallery rhythm.
Metadata is typographic rather than iconographic, so the cards are calmer but require reading labels instead of scanning symbols.
The drawer centralizes secondary controls; this protects the masthead but adds one tap for filter discovery.
